land.text: Saba's last Cliopatria shape, the Marib country with Najran and the Jawf

successors.note: Sabaeans page: 'finally permanently conquered by the Himyarites around 275 CE'; Himyar page: 'around 280'. Cliopatria keeps the Sabaean row to 282 and starts a larger Himyarite shape in 283. Himyar had already conquered Saba once c. 25 BCE and Saba had broken away c. 100 CE.

capitals.name: Ma'rib (Marib)
capitals.note: the page (paraphrase) has the heartland at Marib and Sirwah, with Marib the main urban centre; a secondary capital 'was founded at Sanaa' in the 1st-3rd centuries CE (Sanaa, 44.20 E 15.36 N). Coordinates are the gazetteer's Marib.

keyframe_review.note: 15,044 km2 (43.9-45.9 E, 15.1-16.0 N), -800..-701: the Marib-Sirwah heartland the page names. The page gives no numeric area, so the shape cannot be compared with an infobox figure. The page's beginning is between c. 1000 and c. 800 BCE (paraphrase).

17,090 km2, -700..-676: the heartland grown 2,000 km2 eastward (to 46.5 E). The pages date no Sabaean gain in these years; Karib'il Watar is 'late 8th and early 7th centuries BCE' (Sabaeans) or 'late 7th century' (Karib'il Watar page), so the growth may be an early step of his campaigns.

55,243 km2 (42.5-46.5 E, 15.1-17.8 N), -675..-551: the shape reaches Najran and the Jawf, the northern conquests of Karib'il Watar (the page, paraphrased, has his campaigns extend Sabaean territory to Najran; he besieged the Minaean city of Nashaq three years, Karib'il Watar page). The Gulf of Aden coast and the Hadhramaut foothills the page also credits to him lie south of the shape (min 15.07 N). The two pages put him in the late 8th/early 7th century and the late 7th, so -675 is Cliopatria's year. No infobox area.

63,948 km2, -550..-451: +8,700 km2 over the previous shape, within the 6th century when 'Qatabān had come under the control of Saba' (Qataban page); the Qataban land is drawn as direct territory here, as Cliopatria does. Dated only to the century.

correction.text: Unchanged shape, held to 421 instead of 384

keyframe_review.note: 63,948 km2, -450..-384, identical to the previous shape. 'Qatabān regained its independence in the late 5th century BCE' (Qataban page), so the Qataban land leaves the shape in -420 and a new keyframe takes over. Years only for this shape: -450..-421.

New keyframe -420..-384: the -450 shape without the Qataban core, after the late 5th-century independence of Qataban ('Qatabān regained its independence in the late 5th century BCE'). The year -420 is the researcher's placement within 'late 5th century'. Cliopatria's Qataban row begins in -350.

36,027 km2 (42.7-46.5 E, 15.1-16.4 N), -383..-351: the northern strip (Jawf and Najran) has gone, as Nashshan 'was absorbed under the dominion of the Kingdom of Ma'in between the 6th and 4th centuries BC' (Minaeans page). Cliopatria's Minaean row begins in -383. No page gives the year.

35,605 km2, -350..-111. The Hadhramaut page: 'Hadhramaut became independent from Sheba in c. 330 BCE' (the ledger's vassal_end); the History of Yemen page: 'By the 3rd century BC, Qataban, Hadramout and Ma'in became independent from Saba'. The shape itself is unchanged and no page contradicts it.

35,127 km2, -110..-67, essentially the previous shape (-1.3 percent). The Qataban page: Himyar 'seceded from [Qataban] around 110 BCE and joined Saba to form the kingdom of Saba and Dhu-Raydan' (ledger rename).

correction.text: Saba as before: the -110 shape unchanged for -66..-51

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -66..-51 for a gap: Cliopatria gives these years to a 334,765 km2 Himyarite shape and no Sabaean shape. The Himyar page dates Himyar's conquest of Saba to 'c. 25 BCE (for the first time)', so Saba is still a state in -66..-51; the -110 shape is the bridging judgment (confidence 1). The me-06 dossier (himyarite-kingdom) must reconcile Cliopatria's Himyarite -66..-37 shape.

correction.text: Saba with the Jawf and Najran regained: the -31 shape from 50 BC

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -50..-32: 'The Sabaeans regained their control over Ma'in after the collapse of Qataban in 50 BC' (History of Yemen), so the larger -31 shape (54,376 km2, with the Jawf and Najran) applies from -50; Cliopatria brings it back only in -31. Replaces the -36 shape for -36..-32.

correction.text: Use the -31 shape (with Ma'in's country) for -36..-32

keyframe_review.note: 35,942 km2, -36..-32: the smaller shape without the Jawf. Superseded by the new -50..-32 keyframe: 'The Sabaeans regained their control over Ma'in after the collapse of Qataban in 50 BC'.
54,376 km2, -31..-26: Saba with the Jawf and Najran. 'By the time of the Roman expedition to Arabia Felix in 25 BC, the Sabaeans were once again the dominating power.'

correction.text: Unchanged shape, held to -25 instead of -20. Himyarite Kingdom page: "The kingdom conquered neighbouring Saba' in c. 25 BCE (for the first time)"

keyframe_review.note: 28,196 km2, -25..-20: a Sabaean remnant; Cliopatria's Himyarite shape takes everything from -19 (334,765 km2). The Himyar page dates the first conquest of Saba to 'c. 25 BCE', so the remnant outlasts the page's conquest by five years; the ledger puts the absorption in -25. Reviewer (me-04-b): verdict changed from ok to adjust so that the keyframe agrees with the -25 merge (/ledger/15); years only, -25..-25.

correction.text: The 154 shape for 100..153: Saba independent again, with the Jawf and Najran

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 100..153: Saba 'freed itself from Himyar by around 100 CE' (Sabaeans page); the Himyar page has Saba and Qataban 'split from the Kingdom of Ḥimyar' in the early 2nd century AD. Cliopatria brings a Sabaean shape back only in 154 and shows the Himyarite shape shrinking from 334,765 to 149,074 km2 in 106; the 154 shape is used.

63,917 km2, 154..237. Saba independent of Himyar since c. 100 and, in the page's words, it 'flourished for another century and a half'. The Aksum page has the Sabaean king in conflict with Aksum c. 210-230 (ledger contest).

27,983 km2, 238..246: the Najran/Tihama side is lost while Cliopatria's Aksum row has a Yemeni shape (238..352). The Aksum page dates Aksumite interference in Arabia to c. 200-230 (GDRT) and 'significant territorial expansion in ... the Arabian Peninsula' to c. 240-260 (Monumentum Adulitanum); it gives no frontier. Kept as Cliopatria's (unverified).
63,917 km2, 247..269: the shape returns to the full extent; no page dates the Aksumite withdrawal beyond a statement that Sabaean pressure eventually pushed Aksumite forces back.

correction.text: Unchanged shape, held to 275 instead of 282

keyframe_review.note: 63,917 km2, 270..282. The Sabaeans page: Saba was 'finally permanently conquered by the Himyarites around 275 CE'; the Himyar page says 'around 280'; the History of Yemen page has Shammar Yahri'sh conquering Hadramout, Najran and Tihama in 275. Years only: 270..275.

region.text: the heartland around Marib and Sirwah

ledger.note: c. 800: the Sabaean kingdom at Marib. Saba 'existed in Yemen before 275 CE'; the page (paraphrase) puts its beginning between c. 1000 and c. 800 BCE and cites estimates near 1200, with the heartland at Marib and Sirwah; the History of Yemen page says 'from at least the 11th century BC'. -800 is Cliopatria's first Saba shape and the lower end of the page's range.

region.text: the Jawf: Nashshan and Nashaq, the Minaean cities besieged by Karib'il Watar

ledger.note: 7th century: Karib'il Watar conquers the Jawf. His soldiers attack the Minaean cities Nestum (Nasha'an) and Nescus (Nashaq); he 'besieged the city of Nescus' for three years; Nashshan was forced to accept tribute and the cult of Almaqah (Sabaeans page, paraphrase). The Sirwah inscription gives the campaigns, undated: 'fl. late 7th century BCE' (this page), 'late 8th and early 7th centuries BCE' (Sabaeans page). -675 is Cliopatria's shape change.

region.text: Najran

ledger.note: 7th century: Najran. Karib'il Watar's campaigns the page (paraphrase) has the campaigns extend Sabaean territory to Najran, the Gulf of Aden and the western foothills of the Hadhramaut plateau; 'The last ever campaign was to north of Al Jawf near Najran' (Karib'il Watar page). The Gulf of Aden coast is not in Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: the Hadhramaut kingdom

ledger.note: 7th century (page silent on the year): Hadhramaut under Saba. the Sabaeans page (paraphrase) has Karib'il Watar conquer Awsan, Qataban and Hadhramaut; but the Awsan page has Qataban and Hadhramaut as Saba's 'other allies at the time' of Awsan's fall, and the page itself says that after the 6th century Saba could not keep its supremacy against them. The Hadhramaut page's 'independent from Sheba in c. 330 BCE' ends it. Year placed with the Jawf campaigns; drawn as a tributary tint only if a gap-filler confirms the relation.

region.text: the Kingdom of Awsan, centred on Wadi Markha in Shabwah Governorate

ledger.note: late 7th century: Saba destroys Awsan. 'In the late 7th century BC, this alliance changed into a rivalry' (it had been an alliance in the 8th century); Karib'il Watar obliterated Awsan ('Sabaean inscriptions claim that 16,000 were killed and 40,000 prisoners were taken'); the inscription's closing line has Saba settle its own people in the captured Awsanite lands. The year is placed in the century. The History of Yemen page dates the eight campaigns to the 7th century BC.

region.text: the Kingdom of Awsan, centred on Wadi Markha in Shabwah Governorate

ledger.note: late 7th century: the Awsan land is divided. 'There is also evidence that Saba, after defeating Awsan, divided the territory between two of its other allies at the time: Qataban and Hadhramaut.' The page gives neither shares nor a separate date. Qataban's part; Awsan 'retained its individuality ... at least in the area under Qatabanian control'.

region.text: the Kingdom of Awsan, centred on Wadi Markha in Shabwah Governorate

ledger.note: late 7th century: the Awsan land is divided (Hadhramaut's share, the second of the two allies named by the Awsan page).

region.text: Qataban's land

ledger.note: 6th century: Qataban under Saba. 'Qatabān had come under the control of Saba' in the 6th century BCE (page), having been 'initially allies' of Karib'il Watar in the late 7th. Century only; -550 is Cliopatria's shape growth (+8,700 km2).

region.text: Qataban's land

ledger.note: late 5th century: Qataban is independent again. 'Qatabān regained its independence in the late 5th century BCE'; it then 'was able to conquer Ma'in, and soon embarked on a successful expansionist policy against Saba'. The year is placed in the late 5th century; Cliopatria's Qataban row begins in -350.

region.text: the Jawf (Nashshan and Nashaq) and Najran, the northern strip of the -675..-384 shape

ledger.note: 383 (shape's year): the north goes to Ma'in. Nashshan 'was absorbed under the dominion of the Kingdom of Ma'in between the 6th and 4th centuries BC' and 'As the seventh century BCE closed, and the sixth century BCE opened, the alliance with Saba broke down' (Minaeans page). -383 is Cliopatria's year (its Minaean row also begins then); no page dates it.

region.text: the Hadhramaut kingdom

ledger.note: c. 330: Hadhramaut independent. 'Hadhramaut became independent from Sheba in c. 330 BCE', then allied with the Minaeans and Qataban (page). The History of Yemen page says 'By the 3rd century BC, Qataban, Hadramout and Ma'in became independent from Saba'.

c. 110 BCE: Saba and Dhu-Raydan. Himyar 'seceded from [Qataban] around 110 BCE and joined Saba to form the kingdom of Saba and Dhu-Raydan' (page); Cliopatria begins a Himyarite row in -110. The Himyar page has Himyar independent after 110 and conquering Saba c. 25 BCE.

region.text: Ma'in's country, the Jawf and Najran strip regained

ledger.note: 50 BC: Ma'in regained. 'The Sabaeans regained their control over Ma'in after the collapse of Qataban in 50 BC.' Qataban's end is dated to the late 1st century CE by the Qataban page, so the History of Yemen page's date is its own. Cliopatria brings the larger shape back in -31.

region.text: Marib, the siege 'quickly given up'

ledger.note: 26/25 BCE: Rome invades. The Romans 'attempted to conquer Saba around 26/25 BCE' under Aelius Gallus, prefect of Egypt 26-24 BC (Aelius Gallus page): Najran after fifty days' march, then Asca, Athrula and Marsiaba (Marib, per Ferrero); History of Yemen page: 'the Roman expedition to Arabia Felix in 25 BC'.

region.text: Marib

ledger.note: 25 BCE: the Roman invasion fails. 'Due to heat exhaustion, the siege had to be quickly given up' (Sabaeans page); the Aelius Gallus page: the expedition 'turned out to be a complete failure', 'destroyed the greater part of the army', six months in Arabia and a sixty-day retreat to Alexandria. Trade was rerouted to the sea, weakening Saba economically (Sabaeans page).

region.text: the Sabaean kingdom

ledger.note: c. 25 BCE: Himyar conquers Saba. The Himyar page has the kingdom conquer neighbouring Saba (spelled with a final apostrophe there) 'in c. 25 BCE', 'for the first time'. Sabaeans page: 'Greatly economically weakened, the Kingdom of Saba was soon annexed by the Himyarite Kingdom' (no date). Cliopatria keeps a Sabaean remnant to -20 and gives the Himyarite row everything from -19.

region.text: the Sabaean kingdom regained from Himyar

ledger.note: c. 100: Saba breaks from Himyar. Saba 'freed itself from Himyar by around 100 CE'; the Himyar page has Saba and Qataban 'split from the Kingdom of Ḥimyar' in the early 2nd century AD. Cliopatria's Himyarite shape shrinks in 106 and the Sabaean row returns in 154.

region.text: western Yemen: the Tihama, Najran, al-Ma'afir and Zafar

ledger.note: c. 210: Saba and Aksum collide. GDRT of Aksum, 'the first king to be involved in South Arabian affairs', held much of western Yemen (Tihama, Najran, al-Ma'afir, Zafar) and made a pact with the Sabaean king ʿAlhan Nahfan (page); 'Sabaean and Aksumite interests came into conflict' c. 210-230 under ŠaʿirumYawtar (the page's spelling).

region.text: western Yemen: the Tihama, Najran, al-Ma'afir and Zafar

ledger.note: c. 230: Aksum pushed back. Sabaean pressure Sabaean pressure eventually pushed Aksumite forces back (page, paraphrase; no exact date); Aksumite control of Zafar lasts 'until c. 230'.

region.text: the strip Cliopatria takes from Saba in 238

ledger.note: 238 (shape's year): the west and north go to Aksum. Cliopatria's Sabaean shape shrinks to 27,983 km2 as its Aksum row begins a Yemeni shape (238..352); the Aksum page speaks of Aksumite expansion 'in the Arabian Peninsula' c. 240-260 and 'fighting in Arabia' later in the century, without a frontier.

region.text: the strip restored to Saba in 247

ledger.note: 247 (shape's year): the strip returns. Cliopatria restores the full shape in 247; the Aksum page gives no date for the Aksumite withdrawal.

region.text: the Sabaean kingdom's last shape

ledger.note: c. 275: Himyar conquers Saba for good. Saba 'was finally permanently conquered by the Himyarites around 275 CE'; Himyar page: 'finally conquered the Sabaean Kingdom around 280', 'By 300, the Himyarite Kingdom had vanquished other political units (including the Saba, Qataban, and Hadrawat kingdoms)'. The History of Yemen page: 'It was not until 275 that Shammar Yahri'sh conquered Hadramout and Najran and Tihama.'

region.text: the Sabaean kingdom

ledger.note: c. 275: the Sabaean kingdom ends (the kingdom 'existed in Yemen before 275 CE'). Cliopatria's Sabaean row runs to 282 and its Himyarite shape widens in 283.

wars.name: Karib'il Watar's campaigns

zones.text: the Kingdom of Awsan, centred on Wadi Markha in Shabwah Governorate

wars.outcome: Awsan destroyed ('16,000 were killed and 40,000 prisoners were taken') and its land divided between Qataban and Hadhramaut; Nashshan made to pay tribute; the Jawf and Najran taken.
wars.note: Dated only to the 7th century (History of Yemen: eight campaigns, paraphrase); the Sabaeans page says 'late 8th and early 7th centuries', the Karib'il Watar and Awsan pages 'late 7th century'.

wars.name: Qatabanian-Hadramawt coalition against Saba
wars.outcome: No result recorded: the Qataban page says only that at one point in the 1st century BCE Qataban formed a coalition with Hadramawt, Radman and Madhay against the Sabaeans and gives no details.
wars.note: Years span the century because the page dates it no closer.

wars.name: Aelius Gallus' expedition to Arabia Felix
wars.outcome: A complete failure: the siege was given up and most of the army lost; trade moved to sea routes.
wars.note: The Aelius Gallus page gives no year for the expedition (prefect of Egypt 26-24 BC); the Sabaeans page says 26/25 BCE, History of Yemen 25 BC.

wars.name: Sabaean-Aksumite conflict

zones.text: western Yemen: the Tihama, Najran, al-Ma'afir and Zafar

wars.outcome: Aksum, which had held much of western Yemen with a Sabaean pact, was pushed back by Sabaean pressure.

wars.name: Sabaean-Himyarite wars
wars.outcome: Himyar conquered Saba c. 25 BCE, Saba broke free c. 100 CE, and Himyar prevailed after a long, sporadic civil war among Yemenite dynasties (page, paraphrase), conquering Saba finally c. 275.
wars.note: Not a continuous war: Saba was under Himyar c. 25 BCE-c. 100 CE (Himyar page).

certainty.note: All Sabaean frontiers are approximate; no page gives a boundary, and the Gulf of Aden coast and Najran/Jawf extents rest on inscription claims.

sources.title: Sabaeans
sources.note: State article: Marib, Karib'il Watar, Awsan, Roman expedition, Himyar annexations, 100, 275; no area.

sources.note: Sirwah inscription and campaigns (Awsan, Nashaq, Najran); few dates.

sources.title: Awsan

sources.title: Kingdom of Aksum
sources.note: Aksumite intervention in Yemen c. 200-230 and c. 240-260.

notes:
Page budget up to 9 pages; ten were opened (the Hadhramaut page was used for the c. 330 vassal_end). Three spellings of the Shammar Yuhar'ish article would not load (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shammar_Yuhar%CA%BFish, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shammar_Yuhar%27ish and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shammar_Yuharish); the Himyar page and History of Yemen carried the end. No page gives an area, so the 15 Cliopatria areas are unchecked.

Split decision: the Cliopatria row Sabaeans -800..282 is one state (the kingdom of Saba, with a break c. 25 BCE-c. 100 CE under Himyar) and is kept as one dossier. Cliopatria assigns -66..-37 and -19..153 to the Himyarite row (334,765 km2) and has no Sabaean shapes there; the pages put Himyar's first conquest of Saba c. 25 BCE and Saba's independence c. 100 CE, so new Sabaean keyframes fill -66..-51 and 100..153 and the Himyarite row of me-06 must be checked for the same years.

Open points for a gap-filler: (1) The Karib'il Watar campaigns are dated 'late 8th and early 7th century' (Sabaeans), '7th century BC' (History of Yemen) and 'late 7th century' (Karib'il Watar, Awsan pages); year -675 for the northern conquests (Cliopatria's change) and -625 for Awsan are placements, not pages' dates; the Hadhramaut dossier's gain of the Awsan share is -625 (confidence 2). (2) The Hadhramaut vassal pair (-675 to -330) rests on 'He conquered ... Hadhramaut' and 'independent from Sheba in c. 330 BCE' against the Awsan page's 'allies' and the Sabaeans page's 'could not keep its supremacy' after the 6th century: confidence 1 on the start; the rendering should not tint Hadhramaut until confirmed. (3) The -50 gain (History of Yemen) conflicts with the Qataban page's end of Qataban in the late 1st century CE. (4) The -420 Qataban loss is placed in the 'late 5th century'. (5) 238..246: Cliopatria's Aksum row and the Saba reduction rest on shapes, not pages. (6) Cliopatria's Saba-Minaean relation after -36 (Minaeans shape 84,538 km2 in Yemen only) is not supported by the pages opened.

Counterparts without a dossier: Awsan (8th-7th century BC, Wadi Markha, Hagar Yahirr), Nashshan and Nashaq (Jawf city-states). Region names the gazetteer lacks: Awsan, used as a region name (a real kingdom; the Awsan page puts it on Wadi Markha in Shabwah Governorate; 'Markha' in the gazetteer is a different river).
